title: Usage credits and expedited patch tiers experiment for private deployments
creator: Lena Kim
description:
Summary: Run a structured experiment to validate a two-dimensional packaging approach for Private/VPC and on-prem customers: (A) a base annual license fee + volume-based 'consumption credits' model for GPU hours and support operations; (B) an 'expedited patch & response' support tier that offers defined accelerated upgrade/patch windows and SLA-backed emergency patching with ops credits burn rate. Goal is to find a sustainable balance between predictable recurring revenue, reduced sales friction during procurement, and manageable operational load from urgent on-prem patch windows.

Background & motivation: We consistently hear from large customers that they want predictable baseline fees for budgeting, but also the flexibility to pay for occasional bursts (e.g., emergency patches, on-call support, major upgrade assistance). Current offerings are either flat locked-price support bands (which block deals due to sticker shock) or fully custom SOWs that are slow to negotiate. We propose an experiment that standardizes a credit currency for ops and patches, plus defined support-velocity tiers (Standard / Accelerated / Critical) that map to credits.

Experiment design:
- Offer model A: annual license (base fee) + X consumption credits per year (credits can be used for GPU-hours beyond reserved capacity, patch work, upgrade assistance).
- Offer model B: annual license with a bundled 'accelerated patch tier' (monthly smaller fee) that guarantees 48h, 24h, or 6h response windows depending on tier, and reduces credit burn for emergency activities.
- Cohorts: outbound sales pilot (4 enterprise prospects, mix of regulated industries), inbound self-serve upsell (customers with >$200K ARR), and one internal controlled cohort (existing private deploy customer willing to trial).
- Measurement window: 90 days after contract signature.

Success metrics (primary & secondary):
- Primary: conversion delta (time-to-sign, win-rate) vs. baseline packaging; incremental ARR attributed to new packaging.
- Secondary: ops load (tickets flagged as 'expedited' per cohort), average credits redeemed per customer, legal cycle time for contract review, number of security questionnaires requiring manual responses, and CSAT for upgrade interactions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Achieve >= 12% faster time-to-sign with at least 2/3 of pilot deals compared to baseline.
- Ops load increase limited to <= 25% extra work for accelerated cohort (measured in engineer-hours).
- Security review playbook and templated answers accepted by security team and legal for top 10 OSS questions (see links).

Trade-offs discussed:
- Revenue vs. operational predictability: more generous bundled tiers reduce short-term revenue but can shorten sales cycles.
- Complexity vs. buyer clarity: introducing 'credits' adds mental overhead; mitigated by simple credit buckets and examples.
- Legal and procurement friction for customers with long-run procurement cycles; propose standardized addenda and pre-approved questionnaire templates.

Open questions / decisions needed:
1) Definitive credit exchange rates (e.g., 1 credit = 1 GPU-hour baseline or 1 hour of senior SRE work?).
2) Whether credits can rollover year-to-year.
3) Whether to include an audit log retention tier (additional fee) inside the same packaging experiment, or defer to separate Add-on experiment.

Artifacts and links:
- Pricing spreadsheet (internal): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1private-pricing-spreadsheet-example
- Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/Private+Packaging+Experiment+PRD
- Security Q&A template (Draft): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/Private-SQ-Templates
- GitHub PR for contract addendum draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/contracts/pull/142
- Prototype pricing modal (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/PrivatePricingModalExample

Rollout plan:
- Week 0-2: finalize credit exchange rates and support-velocity definitions; legal pre-approvals for SOW addenda.
- Week 3-6: pilot with 4 targeted prospects (Sales-led) + one internal customer; instrument telemetry for credits and ops tickets.
- Week 7-12: iterate on messaging, heatmap frequently asked security questions and finalize templated responses; collect legal/ procurement feedback.
- Post 90-day review: decide on general availability or iterate for second experiment.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: customers exploit credit model to offload heavy migration work. Mitigation: define 'migration' as out-of-scope or high-burn credit work with clear premium rates.
- Risk: security team bottleneck on questionnaire answers. Mitigation: create pre-approved templates and rotate a single security liaison for pilots.
- Risk: increased emergency SLA load causing burnout. Mitigation: cap number of 'critical' incidents per customer per year, require additional premium for unlimited critical incidents.
